transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me today?

I’ve been feeling constantly restless, like I’m wound too tight and can’t really settle down. Even when I’m supposed to be just sitting calmly in a planning meeting, or doing something relaxing like painting or yoga, I still feel like I can’t fully relax.
How long have you been feeling this constant restlessness—days, weeks, or longer?

It’s been longer than weeks. I’d say it’s been noticeably harder to manage for about two years now—maybe a little over, like two years and a couple months. It seemed to get worse when the conflicts with my in-laws started taking over more of our evenings.
Besides feeling physically restless, do you also find yourself worrying excessively about a number of different things—like work, health, or family—that feels hard to control?

I don’t think so, not in that way. I mean, I have normal worries, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly worrying about a bunch of different things or that it feels out of control. It’s more the restless feeling that stands out to me.
Have you noticed any physical changes along with this restlessness, such as a racing heart, unexplained weight loss, or feeling unusually hot or sweaty?
No, I haven’t really noticed anything like that. My heart doesn’t feel like it’s racing, and I haven’t had unexplained weight loss or feeling unusually hot or sweaty. It’s more just the restlessness.
Over these past two years, have you also noticed feeling persistently sad, down, or losing interest and pleasure in activities you used to enjoy?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed feeling persistently sad or losing interest in things. My mood has been pretty normal overall.
Thinking back to when you were a child or teenager, did you notice similar feelings of restlessness, difficulty sitting still, or trouble focusing before you turned 12?

Yes, I do remember that going back pretty young. In elementary school I’d get notes sent home because I kept popping out of my seat, talking over other kids, and blurting out answers before the teacher even finished asking the question.
